title: Overview
text: What PotDrive is and how the pieces fit together. Portaldot V3 runs TransactionStorage , the pallet behind Polkadot's Bulletin chain. Block producers keep stored data for 100,800 blocks and must prove they still hold it. The node serves it by CID over a bitswap RPC. Before PotDrive there was no SDK, gateway or app for it, and it held no data. PotDrive is the missing layer on top of that pallet: Content-defined chunking FastCDC with chain-level deduplication, so a new version of a file only pays for what changed. One-signature uploads for any number of blocks, through a throwaway in-tab upload key. UnixFS files and folders , including static websites served from the chain. Verified reads everywhere: the Drive, the gateway, the SDK and the CLI re-hash every block. A Solidity registry on Revive for ownership and prepaid keep-alive, called from the same Polkadot wallet. @/components/docs/diagrams

title: Quickstart
text: Store your first file from the Drive, the SDK or the CLI.

title: Before you start
text: Install a Polkadot wallet extension: Talisman, SubWallet or polkadot{.js}. Create an account. Portaldot uses generic Substrate addresses SS58 prefix 42 , which start with a 5. Get test POT. During the Hacker House, the Portaldot team sends tPOT to the native address you register on DoraHacks; otherwise open a ticket in the Portaldot Discord. Storage on the V3 testnet costs about 105 tPOT per MiB, mostly the transaction length fee. A few hundred tPOT covers a handful of small files. See Costs and limits .

title: Use the Drive
text: Open Drive and connect your wallet. Drop a file, or choose Folder to upload a directory or a built website. Review the cost. Blocks Portaldot already holds are listed separately and not charged again. Approve one transaction. PotDrive stores every block, verifies the result from the chain, and returns unspent tPOT. Share the link. Readers verify every block in their own browser.

title: Use the SDK
text: The SDK lives in sdk/src of the repository and runs in browsers, Bun, Node and serverless functions.

title: TransactionStorage
text: How Portaldot holds data: indexing, retention, renewals and storage proofs.

title: The calls
text: Call What it does store data Charges a fee and asks the node to index data under blake2_256 data . Max 8 MiB. renew block, index Re-indexes data stored at block, index for another retention period. Same fee as storing. checkProof proof Inherent included by the block author: proof of a random chunk of the data stored a retention period ago. On Portaldot V3 the pallet is the fee-based variant: there is no authorize_account step, so any funded account can store. We verified this against the live runtime specVersion 3002 : the call list is exactly store , renew and checkProof , and Authorizations is empty.

title: How data is indexed
text: store does not write your bytes into runtime state. It records a TransactionInfo content hash, size, chunk root under the current block, and emits an index operation telling the node's database to keep the extrinsic's data addressable by its blake2b-256 hash. The node later serves it through bitswap_v1_get cid , which accepts any CIDv1 whose multihash is that digest.

title: Why blocks cannot share a batch
text: The database keeps one index entry per extrinsic and stores the last size bytes of the encoded extrinsic sc-client-db , apply_index_ops : Two store calls inside one utility.batchAll would overwrite each other's index entry, and the indexed bytes would not be the data. So every block is its own extrinsic. PotDrive keeps that to one wallet prompt with an upload key .

title: Retention
text: Data is kept for RetentionPeriod = 100,800 blocks, about 7 days at 6-second blocks. When the period ends, the pallet drops the TransactionInfo and validators stop having to hold the data. renew moves it into the renewal block, starting a new period. Anyone can renew any data. PotDrive's keeper does it automatically for prepaid files. You can read what is held at any moment from chain state. Each key of TransactionStorage.Transactions is a block number, and its value lists that block's stored items. Explore renders exactly this.

title: Storage proofs
text: In block N , the author must include checkProof for the data stored at block N − RetentionPeriod . The runtime picks a random 256-byte chunk using on-chain randomness, and the author has to supply that chunk with a trie proof against the stored chunk root. A block with a missing or invalid proof is invalid. Validators that drop data cannot keep producing blocks. Proofs are only required for data stored exactly one retention period earlier. Data stored today is first proven about 7 days later. The proof monitor shows recent blocks and when the next proof falls due.

title: Fees
text: store pays the pallet's own byte and entry fees ByteFee = 10 , EntryFee = 1000 planck, negligible plus the normal transaction fee. On V3 the length component dominates. Measured with paymentInfo on 17 October 2026: Payload Fee 1 KiB 0.1135 tPOT 256 KiB 26.23 tPOT 1 MiB 104.87 tPOT 4 MiB 419.44 tPOT Fees are linear in size, so PotDrive estimates any upload from two paymentInfo calls. They are also the reason deduplication matters.

title: Content addressing
text: Blake2b CIDs, UnixFS DAGs, FastCDC chunking and deduplication.  @/components/docs/diagrams

title: CIDs that Portaldot understands
text: TransactionStorage indexes data under blake2_256 data , and the node's bitswap RPC accepts any CIDv1 whose multihash carries that digest. So every PotDrive block gets a CIDv1 with the blake2b-256 multihash 0xb220 : Block Codec Prefix File leaf raw 0x55 bafk2bzace… File root, directory dag-pb 0x70 bafykbzace… These are standard IPFS CIDs. Any IPFS tool can parse them, and a Portaldot node started with --ipfs-server serves them to IPFS peers over libp2p bitswap.

title: Files as UnixFS DAGs
text: A file that fits in one chunk is a single raw block. Larger files get a UnixFS dag-pb root that links every leaf in order and records each leaf's size in blockSizes . That is the same structure ipfs add --raw-leaves builds, with blake2b instead of sha2-256. Because the root records leaf sizes, a reader can map any byte offset to the leaf that holds it. That is how the gateway answers HTTP Range requests by fetching only the leaves it needs see Gateway .

title: Content-defined chunking
text: Fixed-size chunking cuts every 1 MiB. Insert one byte near the start of a file and every later boundary shifts, so every chunk gets a new hash and has to be stored and paid for again. PotDrive uses FastCDC instead Xia et al., USENIX ATC 2016 . A cut point is where a rolling gear hash of the last ~32 bytes matches a mask. Boundaries follow the content, so an edit only changes the chunks around it. Min / avg / max 256 KiB / 512 KiB / 1 MiB. The 1 MiB cap stays under bitswap's soft block limit. Normalization Harder mask 2^-21 before the average size, easier mask 2^-17 after it. Gear table 256 values from a fixed splitmix32 seed. The table is part of the format: changing it changes every CID. Sp

title: Measured on a 16 MiB file
text: New bytes that had to be stored after each edit run bun scripts/bench-cdc.ts to reproduce : Edit Fixed 1 MiB FastCDC Insert 1 KiB at 300 KiB 16,385 KiB 100% 609 KiB 3.7% Delete 10 KiB at 5 MiB 11,254 KiB 68.7% 343 KiB 2.1% Overwrite 4 KiB mid-file 1,024 KiB 6.3% 898 KiB 5.5% Append 2 MiB 2,048 KiB 11.1% 2,513 KiB 13.6% At about 105 tPOT per MiB, re-uploading that file after a 1 KiB insertion costs roughly 1,680 tPOT with fixed chunks and 62 tPOT with FastCDC. Fixed chunking only wins slightly on pure appends.

title: Deduplication against the chain
text: Before uploading, PotDrive reads TransactionStorage.Transactions once and compares content hashes. Any block Portaldot already holds, from an earlier version, another file or another user, is linked instead of stored. The cost sheet shows reused and new bytes separately, and the upload key only pays for the new ones. Dedup works because the CID is a hash of the bytes. It does not work for private files: each upload is sealed with a fresh key and IV, so identical plaintext gives unrelated ciphertext. That is intentional, since otherwise anyone could test whether you stored a known file.

title: Directories
text: A folder becomes a UnixFS directory: a dag-pb node whose links are named entries, sorted by name. Building the same folder in any order gives the same root CID. Identical files inside it share blocks. Paths resolve one verified block at a time:

title: One-signature uploads
text: The upload key, its lifecycle, and why blocks can't share a batch.  @/components/docs/diagrams

title: The problem
text: Each block must be its own store extrinsic see why . A browser wallet pops up once per signature. Forty prompts for a small website is not a product.

title: The flow
text: Prepare. The browser chunks, hashes and builds the DAG. No network, no keys. Estimate. One state read finds blocks Portaldot already holds. Two paymentInfo calls give the linear fee model. The budget is the fees for new blocks plus 15%, two sweep fees and two existential deposits. Authorize. PotDrive generates an sr25519 key from a fresh mnemonic, in memory. Your wallet signs one utility.batchAll : balances.transferKeepAlive uploadKey, budget , plus revive.call registry, register … if the registry is deployed. Ownership is recorded under your account, not the key's. Store. The upload key sends one store per new block. It pre-assigns nonces and keeps four in flight, and reports each block's i

title: Blast radius
text: The key only ever holds the budget for this upload, and only until the sweep a few blocks later. It has no proxy rights and no registry rights. It is a funded throwaway.

title: Closed tabs
text: Before funding, the mnemonic is written to localStorage with the owner and root. If the tab closes mid-upload, the Drive finds it next time and offers to return the balance. Blocks already stored stay on chain, and re-uploading the same file skips them because they dedupe. Pass a KeyringPair as owner . The same flow runs, and there is no prompt at all.

title: Progress events
text: Event When estimate Fees, reused and new bytes, budget, total. session The upload key's address, before funding. authorized The single wallet transaction is in a block. block Every status change of every block: queued, skipped, sent, inBlock, finalized, failed. verified The root came back over bitswap and matched its hash. swept Unspent budget returned. done The result: root CID, private key if any, block placements.

title: Verification and trust
text: What a reader checks, what it trusts, and what validators prove.

title: Integrity: trust nothing
text: Every read path goes through one function. It asks a node for a block by CID and refuses the bytes unless their blake2b-256 hash equals the CID's digest: A root links its children by CID, so verifying the root and then each child verifies the whole file. A node, the PotDrive gateway or anyone in between can withhold data, but it cannot change data without being caught. On a file page this happens in your browser, straight against the Portaldot node its RPC sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * , and the grid of squares shows each block as it passes.

title: What you still trust
text: Question Who answers Can they lie? Are these the right bytes? Your hash check No Is the data available? The RPC node you query It can withhold. Query another node. When does it expire? Chain state read through that node A dishonest RPC could misreport. A light client or state proof removes this trust. Do validators still hold it? The runtime, via checkProof in every block Not without producing invalid blocks Who owns it? The registry contract No. The record is on chain.

title: Storage proofs
text: For data stored at block N , the author of block N + 100,800 must include a proof of a random 256-byte chunk. PotDrive's proof monitor reads recent blocks, finds the checkProof inherent and the ProofChecked event, and shows when the next proof is due based on the oldest held data.

title: Gasless uploads
text: Upload with 0 tPOT: a relay pays through Portaldot's MetaTx pallet.

title: How it works
text: The Drive prepares the file and generates an in-tab upload key, exactly like a normal upload. Your wallet signs one readable message that authorizes the upload key for one root and a byte budget until a block number: The relay checks that signature raw or wallet-wrapped , then funds the upload key with 0.11 tPOT for its existential deposit and the pallet's tiny per-byte fee. For each block, the upload key signs a meta-transaction for transactionStorage.store . The relay checks that the signer is the authorized key, that the call is store , and that the budget holds. Then it submits metaTx.dispatch and pays the transaction fee.

title: The meta-transaction
text: Portaldot V3's MetaTx extension pipeline, read from runtime metadata: VerifySignature checks a signature over blake2_256 of everything after it: the extension version, the call, then the explicit and implicit data of the remaining extensions. That matches pallet-meta-tx 's own tests.

title: Why the upload key signs, not the wallet
text: Browser wallets wrap any raw message in <Bytes>…</Bytes> before signing it, so they can't produce the bare signature VerifySignature expects. The wallet signs the human-readable authorization instead, and the key it authorizes signs the meta-transactions.

title: Limits
text: Up to RELAY_MAX_BYTES of new data per authorization 256 KiB by default . Deduplicated blocks don't count. Authorizations expire after 300 blocks, about 30 minutes. Sponsored files are not registered, so they have no keep-alive. Re-upload with your own tPOT to register one. The relay is live code, but it needs a funded RELAYER_SEED . Until the deployment's relayer is funded, the Drive hides the Sponsored option. The payload encoding is unit-tested for round-trip and signer recovery, and it is verified against the chain the first time the relayer runs.

title: Versions
text: New versions link to the old one and only pay for blocks that changed.

title: How it works
text: In the Drive, choose New version in a file's details or its right-click menu, then pick the updated file. FastCDC keeps chunk boundaries stable across edits, so most blocks of the new version hash the same as the old one. Portaldot already holds them, so the upload skips them. See the measurements . The registry records parent in the Registered event. Versions form a chain you can rebuild from logs, at no storage deposit. The Drive shows only the latest version in lists, and every version under Versions in the details panel. Each one is still a separate, shareable CID.

title: Private files
text: Client-side AES-256-GCM, the envelope format and share links.

title: How it works
text: PotDrive generates a random 256-bit key and a 96-bit IV with crypto.getRandomValues . It builds a plaintext of a 4-byte header length, a JSON header with the real name and type, then the file. It encrypts with AES-256-GCM through WebCrypto. The 128-bit tag authenticates the whole envelope. The envelope is chunked and stored like any file. The registry records the name as empty and the type as application/octet-stream . The key is base64url-encoded into the link fragment: /f/<cid>#k=<key> .

title: Envelope format
text: Bytes Field 0–3 Magic PDE1 4–15 IV, 12 bytes 16–… AES-256-GCM ciphertext and 16-byte tag over: u32be len ‖ JSON ‖ data

title: Why the fragment
text: Browsers never send the part of a URL after # to a server. Opening a private link loads the page, then the page fetches the ciphertext from Portaldot and decrypts it locally. The PotDrive server, the gateway and the RPC node never see the key or the plaintext. Anyone with the full link can read the file, and links get pasted into chats and indexed by previews. The ciphertext on Portaldot is public and held until it expires, so a leaked key cannot be revoked. Share private links only where you would share the file itself.

title: What still leaks
text: The ciphertext size, within the chunk size. That your account stored something, and when. Nothing else: name, type and content are inside the envelope.

title: Share with a wallet
text: Seal a private file's key to another address with X25519 inbox keys.

title: Inbox keys
text: Polkadot wallets sign but don't decrypt, and sr25519 keys can't be used for key agreement from a browser extension. So each PotDrive user creates an X25519 inbox key on their device. The public half goes into the registry with setInboxKey . The private half stays in that browser. In the Drive this is Receive shared files under Shared with me.

title: Sealing
text: The owner calls share root, to, sealed . The contract checks ownership and emits Shared root, from, to, sealedKey . The recipient's Drive reads Shared logs addressed to their mapped H160, opens each with their inbox key, and lists the files under Shared with me. Binding the root as AAD means a sealed key can't be replayed onto another file. The inbox private key lives in one browser. Lose it and you lose access to files shared with you, though not to files you uploaded. A share is permanent: the sealed key stays in the event log. Sealing to an inbox key is also not revocable, the same as handing over the link.

title: NFTs
text: Mint on Portaldot's native Nfts pallet with media stored on Portaldot.

title: One signature
text: Mint as NFT on a file sends one utility.batchAll : nfts.create and nfts.setCollectionMetadata the first time. Your PotDrive collection is tagged so later mints reuse it. nfts.mint collection, item, you . nfts.setMetadata collection, item, json , with the metadata written straight into chain state. image points at a CID that Portaldot's own validators hold and prove. Anyone can resolve it through any Portaldot node's bitswap_v1_get , or through the gateway.

title: Deposits
text: Collection 1 tPOT once Item 0.1 tPOT Metadata 0.1 tPOT + 0.06 tPOT per byte Deposits are held, not spent, while the collection and item exist. When we checked on 17 October 2026, no Nfts collection existed on the V3 testnet yet.

title: Host a website
text: Deploy a static site as a UnixFS directory and serve it from the chain.

title: Deploy
text: Or use Folder in the Drive. PotDrive builds a UnixFS directory: same input, same root CID, with shared files stored once. Redeploying an edited site only stores the blocks that changed.

title: How it is served
text: /ipfs/<root> redirects to /ipfs/<root>/ so relative URLs resolve. A directory with index.html serves it. Without one, you get a directory listing. /ipfs/<root>/assets/app.js walks the tree one verified block at a time, then serves the file with a type taken from its extension. Files are immutable by CID, so responses carry Cache-Control: immutable .

title: The sandbox
text: Stored HTML, SVG and JavaScript run under Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts allow-forms allow-popups allow-modals allow-downloads , without allow-same-origin . The browser gives the page an opaque origin. It cannot read PotDrive's cookies, storage or wallet session, even though it is served from the same host. The site has no localStorage and no cookies, and same-origin fetch calls count as cross-origin. The gateway sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * , so fetching other CIDs still works. For storage-heavy apps, point a custom domain at a gateway that serves sites on their own origin.

title: Tips
text: Use relative asset paths base: "./" in Vite so the site works under /ipfs/<cid>/ . Hashed asset filenames dedupe well across deploys. Unchanged bundles keep their CIDs. Keep the total under 64 MiB in the Drive. The CLI has no fixed cap, but fees are per byte.

title: Keep-alive
text: Prepaid renewals and the keeper that spends them.

title: Why
text: Portaldot keeps data for 100,800 blocks after it was stored or renewed. Someone has to call renew for every block of a file before that runs out. Anyone can, but nobody remembers to.

title: Prepay
text: Choose 5 or 13 weeks in the Drive, or pass --keep <weeks> to the CLI. The extra value goes into the registry with register as msg.value , held per file. Anyone can top up a file with fund root , so a community can keep a file alive. The owner can withdraw root the remainder at any time.

title: The keeper
text: A Vercel cron calls /api/keeper once a day, authenticated with CRON_SECRET . For each registry file with a balance: Walk the file's DAG and locate every block in TransactionStorage.Transactions . Skip it if the earliest expiry is more than 36 hours away. A daily run leaves a full missed run of slack. Price every renew block, index with paymentInfo . Skip if the balance can't cover it. Send the renewals, then call renewed root, newExpiry, cost to be reimbursed exactly that amount. The contract cannot see native-side renewals, so it trusts the keeper to report the right cost and to have actually renewed. The worst a dishonest keeper can do is take one file's prepaid balance. Every Renewed even

title: Dry run
text: GET /api/keeper?dry runs the whole pass without sending anything and returns what it would do for each file: healthy , renewed , underfunded or expired .

title: MCP server
text: Let AI agents read, store and deploy on Portaldot.

title: Set up
text: Read tools need nothing. Write tools sign with POTDRIVE_SEED and refuse anything over POTDRIVE_MCP_MAX_BYTES per call, so an agent can't run up a bill.

title: Tools
text: potdrive_read Fetch a file or a path inside a stored folder by CID. Every block is verified. Returns text or saves to disk. Opens private files with a key. potdrive_info Every block, where it's held, and when it expires. potdrive_network What TransactionStorage holds right now, and recent storage proofs. potdrive_store Store a local file or inline text, optionally private. Returns CID and link. potdrive_deploy Store a local folder as a site and return its URL.

title: Gateway API
text: HTTP routes, Range requests, headers and status codes.  A file, verified. Raw leaves and UnixFS files. · A directory: index.html if present, otherwise a listing. · A file inside a directory, resolved one verified block per segment. · Adds Content-Disposition: attachment. · Picks the Content-Type from the extension. · JSON: format, every block's block, index, size , expiry and registry record. · JSON: every TransactionStorage entry and the public registry records. · JSON: recent blocks' storage proofs and the next due block.

title: Range requests
text: The gateway reads the UnixFS root's blockSizes , works out which leaves overlap the requested range, and fetches only those. A video can seek to minute 40 without downloading minutes 1 to 39. Responses over 32 MiB are served in windows with 206 Partial Content . Browsers continue with further ranges on their own.

title: Response headers
text: Content-Type From ?name or the path extension, then the registry, then the first bytes. Sealed files are always application/octet-stream . Content-Security-Policy sandbox allow-scripts … for HTML, SVG and JS. See the sandbox . Cache-Control public, max-age=31536000, immutable . A CID never changes. ETag The CID. If-None-Match gives 304 . Access-Control-Allow-Origin * X-Ipfs-Path The resolved path, as IPFS gateways send it.

title: Status codes
text: 400 Not a CIDv1 with a blake2b-256 multihash. 404 Not held by Portaldot never stored, or expired , or no such path. 416 Range outside the file. 502 The node returned bytes that do not match the CID. Refused. 503 The Portaldot node did not answer.

title: Registry contract
text: PotDriveRegistry on Revive: functions, events and storage layout.

title: Why on Revive
text: The bytes live on the native side, in TransactionStorage. The index lives on Portaldot's EVM side, so any EVM tool can read it with eth_call and eth_getLogs . PotDrive calls it with revive.call inside the same utility.batchAll as the upload, so one Polkadot signature does both. Your EVM identity is your account's mapped H160 from reviveApi.address . Revive runs with AutoMap = true .

title: Interface
text: root is the root block's 32-byte blake2b digest, the same value TransactionStorage writes into content_hash . chunks > 1 means the root is dag-pb , which is how readers rebuild the CID from a record.

title: Storage layout and deposits
text: Revive charges a storage deposit per byte and per item DepositPerByte = 0.06 tPOT , DepositPerItem = 0.15 tPOT . We designed the contract around that: A record is two packed slots: owner | size | flags and chunks | storedAt | expiresAt | keepAlive uint128 . Names, types and listings are event logs, which cost no deposit. Lists are rebuilt with eth_getLogs . Compiled with via_ir and optimizer_runs = 1 . The runtime bytecode is about 3 KB with versions and sharing, down from 7,136 bytes in the first version. Slimming the first version cut the deployment deposit from about 578 tPOT to about 224 tPOT, measured with a reviveApi.instantiate dry run. Versions and shares are events, so they add no p

title: Deploying through Revive
text: Constructor arguments must be appended to the init code, and the data argument of instantiateWithCode must be empty. Passing them separately fails with EvmConstructorNonEmptyData Revive error 54 .

title: Tests
text: Twelve Foundry tests cover ownership, expiry, private-by-default listing, re-registration, empty files, funding by third parties, keeper reimbursement and its cap, owner-only withdraw, transfers, version links, inbox keys and owner-only sharing. Run them with cd contracts && forge test .

title: Security model
text: Threats, what PotDrive does about each, and what it doesn't.  A node or the gateway returns tampered data · Every block is re-hashed against its CID before use. Mismatches are refused 502 . · Readers can query any Portaldot node; the CID is node-independent. · Availability depends on the node · Validators silently drop data · The runtime requires checkProof every block for data stored one period earlier. · A stored website attacks PotDrive users · HTML, SVG and JS are served with a CSP sandbox without allow-same-origin: opaque origin, no cookies or storage. · The share link of a private file leaks · Nothing to do after the fact: the ciphertext is public until it expires. · Someone probes whether you stored a known file · Private files get a fresh key and IV, so ciphertext never repeats or dedupes. · Covered for private files · The upload key is stolen from the tab · It only holds this upload's budget, for a few blocks, then sweeps. · The key is persisted locally and the Drive offers a sweep back to the owner. · Capped per file by its own balance. Every claim is a public Renewed event. Owners can withdraw any time. · Bounded, trusted operator · The gasless relay is abused · Each authorization is wallet-signed, bound to one upload key and root, with a byte budget and an expiry. Only transactionStorage.store is sponsored. · A dishonest RPC misreports expiry or ownership · Ownership is read from the contract; expiry from chain state via the same RPC. · Trusts the RPC; a light client fixes this

title: Threats
text: Threat Mitigation Status

title: Keys
text: Your wallet key never leaves the extension. PotDrive asks it for one signature per upload. Upload keys are generated in the tab from a fresh mnemonic and exist only for one upload. Private-file keys exist only in the share link fragment and in the uploader's local library. The keeper key is a server secret KEEPER_SEED . It can only renew and claim per-file balances.

title: Roadmap
text: Read chain state through a light client smoldot instead of trusting one RPC for placements and expiry. Verify renewals inside the registry with a storage proof, so the keeper needs no trust. Serve stored websites from per-CID subdomains so they get a real origin.

title: Costs and limits
text: Measured fees, sizes, retention and known constraints.  100,800 blocks per store or renew, about 7 days at 6 s blocks · 8 MiB MaxTransactionSize . PotDrive blocks are ≤ 1 MiB · 512 MaxBlockTransactions · Block length normal class · ≈ 0.1135 tPOT per KiB, ≈ 104.87 tPOT per MiB linear; measured 17 Oct 2026 · The same as storing the same bytes · ≈ 224 tPOT refundable code deposit · 64 MiB per file or folder; the CLI has no cap · 32 MiB; larger files are served as ranges

title: Is this permanent storage?
text: No. Portaldot keeps data for a rolling window that someone has to renew. Validators are paid to keep and prove data for a known time, and keep-alive automates the renewing.

title: Can an IPFS node fetch my files?
text: The CIDs are standard. A Portaldot node started with --ipfs-server serves them to IPFS peers over libp2p bitswap. The public testnet node exposes the bitswap_v1_get RPC, which is what PotDrive reads.

title: What if potdrive.anshverma.tech goes away?
text: Nothing is lost. The data is in Portaldot, the CID is in your link, and the SDK or CLI can fetch and verify it from any Portaldot node.

title: Why is storage expensive on the testnet?
text: The transaction length fee dominates. PotDrive can't change it, which is why it chunks by content and dedupes against the chain. Re-uploading an edited file usually costs a few percent of the first upload.
